content.title: About
content.content: Kamut is an ancient wheat species (Triticum turgidum ssp. turanicum) cultivated organically. Puffed kamut is made by heat‑expanding whole grains, preserving most of their nutrients. The product has a light, crunchy texture and a mildly nutty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kamut is one of the oldest cultivated grains, grown in ancient Egypt and present‑day Turkey.
Organic kamut is grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers, making it more environmentally friendly.
The grain contains more protein and fiber than common wheat.
Puffed kamut is often used in gluten‑sensitive diets, although it still contains gluten in a more digestible form.
Kamut has a lower glycemic index compared with regular wheat.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Kamut provides about 15 % protein, supporting muscle maintenance and satiety.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and supports gut health.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Kamut supplies magnesium, zinc, iron, and selenium, essential for metabolism and immunity.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It is rich in thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and folate, which are important for energy production.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytonutrients in kamut help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains gluten
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid this product.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to kamut grain.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: Puffed kamut can be high in calories, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Puffed kamut can be enjoyed as a snack, added to muesli, yogurt, smoothies, baked into bars, or used as a crunchy topping for salads. It also works well in gluten‑free baking recipes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store puffed kamut in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation.
